decisions.quote: In previous literature, spatial–temporal associations has only been established with direct tasks (with both verbal and perceptual stimuli), while no studies employed indirect tasks with perceptual (auditory) stimuli. To further investigate this phenomenon, the current study investigated the occurrence of the STEARC effect 1  in both direct and indirect tasks, across four experiments. Consistently with the original work by Ishihara et al. 1 , we successfully replicated the STEARC effect by employing a direct task in Experiment 1.
decisions.reason: The supplied text explicitly states that Ishihara et al. (2008) only tested a direct timing judgment task where participants explicitly assessed whether the target click was earlier or later than the reference sequence, and that no prior studies had investigated whether the auditory STEARC effect occurs automatically in indirect tasks. Experiment 1 is explicitly designated as the conceptual replication of Ishihara et al. (2008) using a direct task, and the authors state the explicit replication verdict that they successfully replicated the STEARC effect in Experiment 1. Experiments 2, 3a, and 3b do not re-test a finding reported by Ishihara et al. (2008), but instead test a novel extension (automaticity in an indirect timbre-discrimination task where timing is task-irrelevant), so the replication outcome for Ishihara et al. (2008) is successful.

decisions.quote: Experiment 1 was a conceptual replication of the original study, in which participants directly discriminated the onset timing (early vs. late) of a target sound after listening to a sequence of auditory clicks. This experiment successfully replicated the STEARC effect and revealed that the onset timing is mapped categorically. In Experiments 2, 3a and 3b participants were asked to discriminate the timbre of the stimuli instead of directly assessing the onset timing. In these experiments, no STEARC effect was observed.
decisions.reason: The paper tests the occurrence of Ishihara et al.'s (2008) STEARC effect across four experiments using the original direct-task paradigm (Experiment 1) and modified indirect-task versions of the paradigm (Experiments 2, 3a, and 3b). Because the STEARC effect replicated in Experiment 1 but failed to emerge in Experiments 2, 3a, and 3b, aggregating the paper's experiments testing the effect yields a mixed outcome.

scope_review.parent_objection: First reply aggregates Experiment1success and Experiments2/3nulls into mixed. But abstract explicitly says the original STEARC effect has only been established with direct timing tasks and no studies investigated whether it occurs automatically in the auditory modality. Introduction and Discussion distinguish conceptual replication in Experiment1 from a new automaticity question in indirect tasks. Determine whether E2/3 truly retest a finding the supplied evidence says Ishihara2008original reported,or test a new extension/automaticity claim absent from the original. Do not exclude based only on an extension label or changed task; do not include solely because the same broad STEARC phenomenon is studied. Codebook requires actual original finding and corresponding new result; close/conceptual failures count only when they re-test that original finding. Inspect source scope and authors own verdict to resolve successful versus mixed. Original identity and type remain accepted.
